title: "seq() with a decimal step misses the round values"
ref: NUM-03
categories: [Numbers]
impact: silencieux
extrait: '0.3 %in% seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)'
reponse: 'FALSE'
attendu: "`TRUE`, 0.3 is in the printed sequence"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
x <- seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)
x
x[4] == 0.3
0.3 %in% x
```
:::

## Why

`seq()` computes each term as `0 + i * 0.1`. But 0.1 has no exact binary representation, and `3 * 0.1` is not exactly the number R stores for `0.3`. Printing rounds to 7 digits and hides the gap.

Here, three terms out of eleven differ from their "round" value: `0.3`, `0.6` and `0.7`. A `%in%` or an `==` filter on these values fails without warning.

## The fix

Build the sequence from integers, or search with a tolerance.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
y <- (0:10) / 10
0.3 %in% y
any(abs(x - 0.3) < 1e-8)
```
:::
